---
title: Runcrate
description: How to run Axolotl training on a Runcrate GPU instance
---

[Runcrate](https://www.runcrate.ai/?utm_source=axolotl&utm_medium=directory&utm_campaign=gpu_pricing) rents GPU virtual machines by the hour, from an RTX A6000 up to H100, H200, B200 and B300. Its **Finetune** image (`ubuntu-train`) comes with Docker and the NVIDIA container runtime, so the Axolotl Docker image runs on it without any setup. This guide starts an instance with the `runcrate` CLI, trains a LoRA adapter in the Axolotl image, copies the result back and deletes the instance.

## Setup

Install the [Runcrate CLI](https://www.runcrate.ai/docs/cli/installation?utm_source=axolotl&utm_medium=directory&utm_campaign=gpu_pricing) and sign in:

```bash
curl -sSL https://runcrate.ai/install.sh | sh
export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"
runcrate login
```

The installer puts `runcrate` in `~/.local/bin` (on macOS, in `/usr/local/bin` when that is writable); the `export` line adds it to `PATH` in the current shell. `runcrate login` opens the browser. On a machine without one, set `RUNCRATE_API_KEY` to an API key from **Dashboard > Keys** instead.

## Start an instance

List the machines that have the GPU you want, with their price per hour:

```bash
runcrate instances types --gpu A6000
```

Create the instance with the Finetune image. `--max-runtime` terminates it four hours after it starts running, so a forgotten instance does not keep billing:

```bash
runcrate instances create --name axolotl --gpu A6000 \
  --template ubuntu-train --max-runtime 4h
```

Termination deletes the instance's disk, so pick a limit that covers both training and copying the result back. To give a running instance more time, raise the limit (it counts from the start): `runcrate instances auto-stop axolotl --max-runtime 8h`.

`runcrate instances status axolotl` reports `running` once the instance is ready, usually after a few minutes. You can also create it from the [deploy form](https://www.runcrate.ai/auth/signup?utm_source=axolotl&utm_medium=directory&utm_campaign=gpu_pricing&redirect=%2Fdashboard%2Finstances%3Faction%3Dcreate%26gpu%3DA6000%26template%3Dubuntu-train%26src%3Daxolotl).

## A first run

`runcrate ssh` runs a command on the instance over SSH, with no key setup. Pull the image, then train the bundled `examples/llama-3/lora-1b.yml` config for 10 steps as a trial run:

```bash
runcrate ssh axolotl -- docker pull axolotlai/axolotl:main-latest

runcrate ssh axolotl -- "docker run --gpus all --ipc=host --rm \
  -v /root/outputs:/workspace/axolotl/outputs \
  axolotlai/axolotl:main-latest \
  axolotl train examples/llama-3/lora-1b.yml --max-steps 10"
```

- The image's working directory is its Axolotl checkout, so the example configs are available by relative path. Its entrypoint sets up the CUDA libraries, so pass the `axolotl` command directly rather than replacing the entrypoint.
- `-v /root/outputs:/workspace/axolotl/outputs` keeps the adapter on the instance after the container exits. The config writes it to `./outputs/lora-out`.
- Drop `--max-steps 10` to train for the epochs set in the config.
- For gated models, add `-e HF_TOKEN=<token>` to `docker run`.

To train your own config, copy it to the instance and mount it into the container. Set `output_dir` in the config to a path under `./outputs/` (for example `./outputs/my-run`) so the result lands in the mounted `/root/outputs` and survives `--rm`:

```bash
runcrate ssh axolotl -- mkdir -p /root/configs
runcrate cp ./my_training.yml axolotl:/root/configs/my_training.yml

runcrate ssh axolotl -- "docker run --gpus all --ipc=host --rm \
  -v /root/configs:/configs -v /root/outputs:/workspace/axolotl/outputs \
  axolotlai/axolotl:main-latest \
  axolotl train /configs/my_training.yml"
```

Long runs keep going if your terminal disconnects when you start the container with `-d` instead of `--rm` and follow it with `runcrate ssh axolotl -- docker logs -f <container>`.

## Copy the result and clean up

Copy the adapter back, then delete the instance to stop billing. Everything on the instance's disk is deleted with it. For your own config, copy `/root/outputs/<run>` instead:

```bash
runcrate cp -r axolotl:/root/outputs/lora-out ./lora-out
runcrate instances delete axolotl
```

## Several GPUs

Create the instance with more GPUs on the same machine, for example `--gpu H100:4`, and launch the multi-GPU configs as described in the [multi-GPU guide](multi-gpu.qmd).
